caveat.notSame: Note: “not significant” does not mean “the same” – a small sample can hide a difference.
caveat.cause: The result describes an association, not a cause.
caveat.expected: The test assumes expected counts of at least 5 in most cells.

ttest.indSig: **{{variable}}** **differs significantly** between the groups – it is higher for {{higher}} ({{stats}}).
ttest.diffSig: The difference of {{diff}} in favour of {{higher}} is {{size}} (d = {{d}}).
ttest.leveneOk: Levene's test ({{p}}) does not suggest unequal variances, so the first table row applies.
ttest.leveneWelch: Levene's test ({{p}}) shows unequal variances, so the second table row (Welch's test) applies.
ttest.pairedNs: There is **no significant difference** between **{{a}}** and **{{b}}** ({{stats}}).
ttest.pairedDiff: The mean change of {{diff}} is a {{size}} effect (dz = {{d}}).
ttest.oneSig: The mean of **{{variable}}** ({{mean}}) is significantly **{{dir}}** than {{value}} ({{stats}}).
ttest.oneNs: The mean of **{{variable}}** ({{mean}}) does **not differ significantly** from {{value}} ({{stats}}).
ttest.oneDetail: M = {{mean}}, SD = {{sd}}, n = {{n}}; the difference is {{size}} (d = {{d}}).

anova.sig: The means of **{{variable}}** **differ significantly** between the groups ({{stats}}).
anova.ns: The means of **{{variable}}** do **not differ significantly** between the groups ({{stats}}).
anova.range: The highest mean is in {{hi}} ({{mhi}}), the lowest in {{lo}} ({{mlo}}).
anova.eta: The groups explain {{pct}} % of the variance (η² = {{eta}}), a {{size}} effect.
anova.posthoc: A post hoc test (e.g. Tukey) in the ANOVA dialog shows which groups differ.
anova.levene: Levene's test ({{p}}) shows unequal variances – treat the result with care, or use the Kruskal-Wallis test.

corr.noneSig_other: None of the {{count}} correlations is significant.
corr.posMeaning: A positive relationship means higher values of one variable tend to go with higher values of the other.

crosstab.sig: There **is a significant association** between the variables in **{{title}}** ({{stats}}).
crosstab.ns: There is **no significant association** between the variables in **{{title}}** ({{stats}}).

reg.r2: Together the predictors explain {{pct}} % of the variance of {{dependent}}.
reg.pred: {{name}}: each extra unit {{dir}} the prediction by {{b}} ({{stats}}).

freq.top: The most frequent value of **{{variable}}** is **{{top}}** ({{pct}} % of valid answers).

mw.sig: **{{variable}}** **differs significantly** between the groups – {{higher}} has higher ranks ({{stats}}).
mw.ns: **{{variable}}** does **not differ significantly** between the groups ({{stats}}).

kw.ns: **{{variable}}** does **not differ significantly** between the groups ({{stats}}).

wx.sig: There **is a significant difference** between the measurements **{{label}}** ({{stats}}).
wx.ns: There is **no significant difference** between the measurements **{{label}}** ({{stats}}).

chi1.sig: The categories of **{{variable}}** are **not equally represented** ({{stats}}).
chi1.ns: The distribution of **{{variable}}** does **not differ significantly** from an even one ({{stats}}).
chi1.detail: {{over}} is most above expectation, {{under}} most below.

rel.line: Cronbach's alpha is **{{alpha}}** for {{items}} items – internal consistency is **{{quality}}**.
rel.detail: Values from .70 are usually considered acceptable, from .80 good.
rel.tooHigh: An alpha above .95 may mean the items are redundant.
